lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Describing Movement on a Grid
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 2, Session 3
lesson.fileName: Session 3 - Describing Movement on a Grid.pptx

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Space, Year 5 (VC2M5SP02): coordinates and directional language to describe position and movement; Year 6 (VC2M6SP02): describe changes to the coordinates when a point moves
plan.shape: problem-first: students move a point before the rule is named, because most can move a point and the gap is saying which number changes
plan.criticalFeature: left and right change the first number; up and down change the second
decisionPoints: the hinge: describe the move from two points
plan.anchor: across the corridor, then up the stairs: (x, y), and the numbers sit on the lines
plan.catchUp: Missed Sessions 1 or 2? Plot one point together with the anchor, then start at the launch: moving is reading a point twice.

studentTools: A ruler and a sharp pencil for every student
A counter for every pair, to move on the grid
Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: across the corridor, then up the stairs, (x, y)
Under it: left and right change the first number; up and down change the second

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. A table of moves, sliding a triangle, describing moves, a mistake to fix and a robot delivery problem.
resources.title: Describing Movement on a Grid
resources.subtitle: Left and right change the first number. Up and down change the second.

example.prompt: (2, 3) moves 4 right. Where does it land?

items.prompt: Slide the triangle 3 right. Draw it in its new place and write its new corners.
Look at your triangle. Which number changed in every corner? Which stayed the same?
items.answer: The first (across) number went up by 3 in every corner. The second number stayed the same.

steps: The first number went from 1 to 5: 4 right.
The second number went from 2 to 6: 4 up.

items.prompt: Kai moved the point (4, 2) up 3. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: Up changes the second number, so it is (4, 5). Kai changed the across number.

example.prompt: A robot at (0, 0) moves 3 right, then 2 up. Where is it?

items.prompt: A delivery robot moves around the school map.
A robot starts at (0, 0). Which path ends at (4, 4)?
items.explain: Both: the right moves add 4 to the first number and the up moves add 4 to the second, in either order.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Sliding a rectangle, a repeating move pattern and your own path, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Moving Shapes and Patterns
resources.subtitle: Move every corner the same way.

example.prompt: Slide the corner (1, 1) 2 right and 3 up.

items.prompt: A rectangle slides 2 right and 3 up. Fill in its new corners.

example.prompt: A point starts at (0, 0) and keeps moving 1 right and 2 up. Where is it after 2 moves?
steps: The second number is always double the first.

items.prompt: A point starts at (0, 0) and keeps moving 2 right and 1 up. Write its next four positions.
Will that point ever land on (10, 5)?
items.explain: Yes: after 5 moves it is at (10, 5), because 5 lots of 2 right is 10 and 5 lots of 1 up is 5.

items.prompt: Will it ever land on (7, 3)? Explain.
items.answer: No. The first number is always even (2, 4, 6, 8...), so it never reaches 7.

steps: The first number goes 1 to 5: 4 right.

items.prompt: Plot 4 places of your choice on squared paper. Write a path of moves that visits all four and comes back to the start. Check your moves add back to zero.
items.answer: Check the moves: total right equals total left, and total up equals total down.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: the arrow is drawn, and a hint says which number changes.
resources.title: Moving Points: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Count the squares as you move.

example.prompt: A is at (1, 2). It moves 3 right.
D is at (2, 1). It moves 3 up.

slides.notes: Session 3 of our coordinates week: today we describe how points move on a grid.
Before you start, put boards, markers, a ruler, a pencil and one counter per pair on desks. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Decimal to fraction
prompts: Write 0.35 as a fraction in its simplest form.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with fractions, decimals and percentages from last term.
ASK: How do you write 0.35 as a fraction in its simplest form?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7/20
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> shade the hundred grid: 35 hundredths,
then divide top and bottom by 5. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 0.35 is 35 hundredths, and that simplifies to 7 twentieths.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: stopping at 35/100.
Fix: find a number that divides both, and they simplify it.
notes.prep: Review of Term 3 fractions, decimals and percentages (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 30 percent of 80?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 24
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> find 10 percent first, 8, then times 3. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent of 80 is 8,
so 30 percent is 24. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 30 or 50.
Fix: find 10 percent first, and they multiply by 3.
notes.prep: Term 3 review: percentage of an amount.

beats: ASK: Can you put these in order from smallest to largest?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> change all three to percentages together, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 38 percent, then two fifths, which is 40 percent,
then 0.45, which is 45 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: putting 0.45 first because it looks small.
Fix: turn each one into a percentage, and they reorder.
notes.prep: Term 3 review: comparing fractions, decimals and percentages.

beats: SAY: Now for our four times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 4 times 12?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 48
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 12, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 48. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 44.
Fix: double 12 to get 24, double again to get 48, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many fours make 28?
ASK: What is 28 divided by 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> halve 28 to 14, then halve again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 7. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 6 or 8.
Fix: halve 28, then halve again, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Here's a bigger one. Use doubling.
ASK: What is 4 times 25?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 100
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> think of four quarters of a dollar. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 100. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 80.
Fix: double 25 to get 50, double again to get 100, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to describe how a point moves on a grid and how its coordinates change.
successCriteria: I can move a point left, right, up or down on a grid.
I can write the new coordinates after a move.
I can explain which number changes and why.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: We can read and plot points now.
Today we move them, and watch what happens to the numbers.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 moving a point is reachable for everyone; SC2 writing the new coordinates is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 explaining which number changes is the stretch.

slides.title: Move the robot
slides.prompt: R moves 3 right. Where does it land?

beats: POINT to R.
SAY: Our robot R is sitting at 2, 3.
Put your counter on it on your grid if you have one.
ASK: If R moves 3 squares to the right, what are its new coordinates?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (5, 3)
SCAN boards for (5, 3).
80%+ -> ask: Which number changed? Which stayed the same?
Less -> move R one square at a time on the big grid,
counting together. Re-ask.
SAY: It lands on 5, 3. Moving right changed the first number,
and the second number stayed the same. That's our big idea today.
trap: writing (2, 6).
Fix: move the counter right, not up, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Problem-first: students move before the rule is named. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: To slide a point or a shape to a new place, without turning or flipping it.

notes.answer: slide to a new place, no turning or flipping
beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is translate. Say it with me: trans-late.
SAY: In maths, translate means slide.
The point or shape moves to a new place, but it doesn't turn or flip.
ASK: Show me a translation with your hand: slide it across your desk.
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three. Slide... now.
EXPECT: every hand slides, no turning
trap: turning the hand as it moves.
Fix: keep fingers pointing the same way, and they slide again.
notes.prep: Translate is the Year 6 word; slide and move are fine in speech. Keep the arrow on the board.

slides.title: Move right or left
steps: Move 4 right: right changes the first number.

beats: MODEL moving P four squares right.
SAY: Let me move P four squares to the right.
I count each square as I slide.
POINT to the first number.
SAY: Moving right takes me further across, so the first number grows by 4.
I'm not going up or down, so the second number stays the same.
ASK: So what are P's new coordinates?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (6, 4)
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 6, 4. Two plus four is six,
and the up number stayed 4.
trap: adding 4 to both numbers.
Fix: ask whether P went up at all, and they fix the second number.
notes.stretch: What move would take P back to where it started?
notes.help: Slide a counter along the grid and count each square.
notes.prep: The critical feature: right and left change only the first number. SC2.

beats: POINT to Q.
SAY: Now Q moves twice: 2 to the left, then 3 down.
MODEL left first.
SAY: Left takes me back across,
so I take 2 from the first number: 5 take away 2 is 3.
ASK: Down changes the other number. So what's the second number now?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 2
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 5 take away 3 is 2. So Q lands on 3, 2.
Left and right changed the first number, and down changed the second.
trap: taking 2 from the second number.
Fix: point to left on the anchor, and they redo the first number.
notes.stretch: Would it matter if Q went down first, then left?
notes.help: Do one move at a time, and write the point after each one.
notes.prep: Two moves, two numbers: each direction belongs to one number. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Where does it land?
slides.prompt: (3, 2) moves 4 up. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: changes the first number for an up move

beats: SAY: Think about which number up changes before you choose.
ASK: If the point 3, 2 moves 4 up, where does it land?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What move would land on A?
Less -> say the anchor again: up the stairs is the second number. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 3, 6. Up changes the second number,
so 2 becomes 6, and the 3 stays.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: walk it on the big grid: up, not across, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A means up was put on the first number; C means both numbers were changed.

slides.title: Where does it land?
slides.pivot: move a counter one square at a time on the grid
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which number changed, and why?

items.text: (3, 6) moves to (3, 2). What was the move?
items.say: It moved 4 down. The across number stayed 3.

say: Write where each point lands on your board.
trap: changing the wrong number.
Fix: point to the anchor:
left and right is the first number, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Write the move that would take the point back to its start.
notes.help: Draw the point on a small grid on your board, then move it.
notes.prep: Guided practice from one move to two moves, an edge case landing on (0, 0), then a reverse question. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
B slid to B dash. Describe the move.
ASK: How did B move to get to B dash?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5 right, 2 down
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> write both points' coordinates first, then compare each number. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It moved 5 right and 2 down.
The first number went from 1 to 6,
and the second from 4 to 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 5 right, 2 up.
Fix: ask whether B dash is higher or lower than B, and they fix it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work: describing a move from two points. Anyone with right and down mixed up starts on the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Move points and describe moves on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which number did that move change?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: changing the wrong number.
Fix: ask which direction belongs to which number, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: sliding a rectangle, a repeating move pattern and planning your own path.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: the arrows are drawn, and a hint says which number changes.
notes.prep: Independent practice: a table of moves, a translation, describing moves, a mistake and a robot problem. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: M moves 3 right and 4 down. Write its new coordinates.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Where does M land after 3 right and 4 down?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (5, 1)
RECORD who changes the wrong number.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing (5, 9) or (6, 2).
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: two moves, with a down move that subtracts.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner which number changes when you move up.

notes.answer: open - listen for the second number, because up is the stairs
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can write the coordinates after a move?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with (5, 9) on the board matters most.
ASK: Which number changes when a point moves up, and why?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: the second number, because up is the stairs
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow's Cartesian plane builds on this.
